title: Lung-CLiP machine learning detects early-stage lung cancer from cell-free DNA
summary: Improved CAPP-Seq cfDNA analysis showed that ctDNA is present before treatment in most early-stage lung cancers and that most cfDNA mutations in patients and risk-matched controls reflect clonal haematopoiesis. Integrating these findings, the lung cancer likelihood in plasma (Lung-CLiP) machine-learning method discriminated early-stage patients from risk-matched controls with performance similar to tumour-informed ctDNA detection.
ai_technology: Lung-CLiP machine-learning classifier integrating cfDNA genomic features

evidence.tested: Described in the abstract as prospectively validated; discrimination of early-stage patients from risk-matched controls.
evidence.unknown: Cohort sizes and validation design not reviewed, so the prospective claim is not classified as frozen-model prospective testing; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning combined cfDNA mutation, fragment and other features into a lung cancer likelihood score.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
